SMS360 · Portfolio work sample

Database specification

Why a notebook belongs to a class and academic year, and how a grade policy belongs to a particular semester.

Adapted from work on SMS360. Examples use fictional records and representative implementation names.

Logical entity relationships

Data dictionary

EntityPrimary keyScope or foreign keysRule
Classclass_idschool_idProvides the notebook’s school scope.
Academic yearacademic_year_idschool contextProvides the year dimension. One year can contain several terms.
Homeroom notebooknotebook_idclass_id + academic_year_idUnique pair. The selected term never creates a new notebook.
Notebook section datasection_record_idnotebook_idChild data for reports, plans and other sections. Term-specific content can carry a reporting checkpoint.
Notebook authorizationassignment_idnotebook_id, user_id, access roleLinks a user to the notebook with page-level access rules.
Notebook auditevent_idnotebook_id, actor_idStores operation, time and a change snapshot.
Grade visibility policyconfiguration_idschool_id + academic_year_id + semester_idUnique policy tuple. Status and JSON flag determine the effective visibility.
Grade policy auditevent_idconfiguration_id, actor_idStores operation, before/after snapshot, time and source channel.

Record lifecycle and constraints

  • On first notebook access, resolve the school-scoped class and year, then create or return the existing notebook under the class-year uniqueness constraint.
  • The term selection determines the reporting content. The class-year key continues to resolve the same notebook.
  • Selector fields and identities originate in the school’s academic data. Existing notebook history remains associated with the original record.
  • Notebook and grade-policy changes have separate audit trails because their scopes and payloads differ.

SQL validation sample

This sample checks the class-year invariant on the illustrative schema.

Duplicate notebook check

SELECT class_id, academic_year_id, COUNT(*) AS notebook_count
FROM homeroom_notebook
GROUP BY class_id, academic_year_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
